sections.content:
Level 1: Top row b,N,Y,p; tray N,p,b,Y (shuffled). So in Level 1 the tray order didn't match the top row order, and I placed them in top row order (b,N,Y,p). So the placement order = top row order, and that worked in Level 1. But was the order actually required, or was it just a coincidence? Unclear.
Current placement order in Level 2: O, p, b, N, R, Y, M (the order I actually placed them). Top row order: O, p, R, b, N, Y, M. So I deviated: I placed b (4th in top row) 3rd, and R (3rd in top row) 5th.
If the order is enforced, I need to redo the placement in the order O, p, R, b, N, Y, M. That requires removing the misplaced pieces. Can I remove a placed piece? Test: select the piece in L3 (red) and click the tray → does it go back to the tray? Or click an empty slot?
But wait — there's a subtle point: if the order is enforced, R (red) must be placed 3rd, into L3 (the pipe slot). And the pipe... hmm, if red is placed in L3 3rd, does the pipe automatically copy it to U3? That didn't happen (red was placed 5th, but maybe the pipe only fires when the piece is placed in the correct order!). This is a consistent theory: the pipe copies the piece in L3 to U3, but only if the placement sequence matches the top row order up to that point.
This is getting pretty speculative. The cleanest test: remove all pieces from the board (if possible), then place them in strict top row order, and press SPACE.
First, test the removal: click the red piece in L3 to select it, then click the tray area (58,31). Check whether red returns to the tray.
Actually, the tray area: the tray markers are the g 4px dots at row 58, columns 10,17,24,31,38,45,52. Clicking (58,31) might return the selected piece to the tray.
Let's test that.
